references.text: Melchizedek uses exactly the same title 'El Elyon, Maker of heaven and earth' in his blessing of Abram – Abram repeats this title in his oath to the king of Sodom.
God raises His hand toward heaven and swears, a parallel to Abram's gesture where he raises his hand in an oath to the Lord.
The book of Hebrews summarizes the episode with Melchizedek and Abram, including the context where Abram acknowledges God Most High.
The angel raises his hand toward heaven and swears by Him who made heaven and earth – a direct parallel to Abram's oath by the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth.
God swears by Himself that every knee shall bow – a parallel to the solemnity of the oath Abram shows before the Lord.
Both verses highlight God's self-revelation as the personal, Almighty God who makes covenants with Abraham.
Both verses illustrate Abraham's humble yet bold relationship in speaking with God Most High.
The verses link together God's names 'Most High' and 'Almighty' in Abraham's life.
Both verses use the specific title 'the Lord, the God of my lord Abraham' to confirm God's covenant with Abraham's household.
Both verses affirm God's sovereignty over all creation, independent of geographical limitations.
Exodus 6:8 refers directly to Abraham's oath with raised hand in Genesis 14:22 as the basis for God's promise of the land.
Both verses use hand gestures as a ritual sign of oath and covenant in Abraham's family.
The verses create a contrast between Abraham's raised hand as an oath to God and the enemy's raised hand as rebellion.
Both verses use the fixed liturgical formula 'the Lord, the God of my lord Abraham' to confirm God's faithfulness.
Both verses show Abraham's use of oaths and promises as binding actions, whether toward God or people.
Both verses confirm God's guidance and faithfulness to the house of Abraham through a fixed liturgical formula.
Both verses confirm God's identity as the creator and owner of heaven and earth.
15:18 formalizes God's covenant regarding the land, which Abram affirms his loyalty to in 14:22.
Both verses confirm God's sovereignty over nations and the earth as the God of Abraham.
